title: Systematic Bias in Large Language Models: Discrepant Response Patterns in Binary vs. Continuous Judgment Tasks
base_benchmarks: Value statements from Moore et al. (2024)
News headlines from Rathje et al. (2024) and Robertson et al. (2023)
Human profiles from GSS agents bank (Park et al., 2024)
findings: The paper did not report specific findings on religion, as 'religious freedom' was only used as an example of a value statement topic. The general finding was that across all topics, LLMs were more likely to deliver negative judgments (e.g., 'oppose', 'No') when using binary response formats compared to continuous scale formats. This implies that for a statement on religious freedom, an LLM would be more likely to show opposition in a binary task than when asked to rate its support on a scale.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured Large Language Models' subjective judgments on value statements. 'Religious freedom' was mentioned as one example of a topic covered in these statements, alongside others like 'income inequality'. The core measurement was the discrepancy in judgments when responses were solicited in a binary format (e.g., support/oppose) versus a continuous format (e.g., a 0-10 scale).
